verdict.reasoning: Patient reports headache 'for a few days' and 'around three days ago' and agrees it is 'getting worse over the last three days.'

Location and quality: 'it kind of feels all over my head, but like mainly, um, around my right eye'; 'it's dull but sometimes it gets a bit sharper.' This supports holocephalic with predominant right peri‑orbital pain and dull with intermittent sharp pain.
She says, 'it kind of comes and goes. Um but, I mean it is there all the time, but like sometimes it's stronger' and rates it 'probably a eight' on a 1–10 scale.

Photophobia: 'now like light is quite annoying, my eyes' and when asked, 'does it hurt to look at bright lights?' she answers 'Yeah, yeah. It hurts.' She also notes 'this like weird shooting lights' at onset.
Doctor asks 'Any nausea or any vomiting?' Patient: 'I'm like basically, I I'm sick with the headache. But I, no vomiting.' Feeling 'sick' with headache implies nausea without vomiting.

She denies loss of vision ('Not loss of vision'), speech difficulty ('Any difficulty ... speaking... ?' 'No.'), weakness ('Any ... weakness in your arms and legs?' 'No.'), neck stiffness and pain ('Any neck pain or neck stiffness?' 'No.' after initial confusion), head injury ('any recent head injuries at all?' 'no.'), fever ('Any temperatures, or fevers?' 'No.'), and rash ('Any rashes at all, on your skin?' 'no').

She works with computers: 'I work in IT. So I work with computers a lot... I had to like reduce the uh, brightness of my screen.' She mentions work stress: 'it's been a bit stressful, kicking off a new project' and suspected dehydration: 'at first I thought it's stress, or maybe I didn't drink enough water... sometimes when I don't drink enough water, I like get headaches.' These are framed as possible triggers.
Impact: 'it's hard to focus though. So, I I had to take a couple of days off work, actually' and 'I work with computers a lot... I had to like reduce the uh, brightness of my screen.'

When asked about other medical history: 'Are you otherwise fit and well... do you have any other medical history?' Patient: 'Yeah, I think so. It's just the headache.' No other conditions are reported.
Patient: 'I tried uh Ibuprofen. Um so I took, like a few. Um for the last two days, basically.' Later: 'How many tablets did you take of Ibuprofen?' 'Uh, three a day.'
When asked, 'do you take any regular medication?' she replies, 'Uh, no no.'
Doctor: 'Do you have any allergies to any medications?' Patient: 'Mm not that I know of.'

Family history: 'my sister and my mom have them [migraines] quite frequently.' She elaborates: 'my sister's... it's very rare. But my mom's is like quite bad... usually when there's like a season changing...' indicating mother’s frequent/seasonal migraines.
Living situation: 'I live with housemates. So, three of them. So we're four.' Work: 'I work in IT. So I work with computers a lot.'
Doctor: 'regarding smoking or alcohol. Do you drink or smoke at all?' Patient: 'I socially smoke. And I drink only socially.'
Glasses: 'Do you wear glasses?' 'Yes, I do.' Eye test: 'Have you had any recent eye check, done? Eye test?' 'No... I've been wearing them since I was five... so, it's quite a long time.'

Doctor’s assessment: 'I do think this could be, a headache very similar to a migraine. The reason I say that is because the history is very suggestive of it, given your mum and your sister also migraines.'

Poor response: 'I tried uh Ibuprofen... But it doesn't really help, no.' Under‑dosed: Doctor says, 'I'm not sure whether you're taking, the correct dose. You can take up to two tablets, three times a day,' after she reports 'three a day.'
Family history: 'my sister and my mom have them quite frequently' and doctor references this: 'given your mum and your sister also migraines.'

Red flags denied: no fever ('Any temperatures, or fevers?' 'No.'), no neck stiffness ('Any neck pain or neck stiffness?' 'No.'), no focal deficits or speech changes ('Any difficulty with speaking... ?' 'No.'; 'Any ... weakness in your arms and legs?' 'No.'), and no trauma ('any recent head injuries at all?' 'no.').
Doctor: 'You can take up to two tablets, three times a day,' explicitly advising optimization of ibuprofen dosing.
Doctor: 'Or, I can prescribe you something stronger, like Naproxen, which is another anti-inflammatory, which can be helpful.'
Doctor: 'We can also add in other, painkillers like, Paracetamol, or Codeine. Which might be helpful as well.'
Doctor: 'It may be worth keeping a headache diary so we can try and work out what's, you know, if there's any triggers which could be causing your headaches to become worse.'

While the patient mentions reducing screen brightness, the doctor does not specifically 'advise screen hygiene including breaks and brightness adjustments.' No explicit recommendation about breaks or screen hygiene is documented.

Doctor: 'Something for you to bear in mind if you feel that you are, your eyes are straining. Um I would always recommend having a repeat eye test done.' This implies optometry review if strain persists.
Doctor: 'I'd like you to come back and see me, in about uh, a week's time, week to two weeks' time.'
Doctor: 'If you are having, more frequent episodes of these type of headaches. We can think about giving you medications as, prophylactic... But we can have that discussion next time.'

Doctor advises: 'if your headaches aren't getting any better, or they're getting worse... give me a call, or come back and see me... if you're having any problems with your vision, or weakness in your arms and legs, or you're just not feeling very well.' Fever and neck stiffness are NOT mentioned in these return precautions; including them as explicit advice adds conditions not stated.
